==================================================
2. LOCKED PRODUCT DECISIONS
==================================================

Ticket state machine:

ONLY these transitions are valid:

OPEN → IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED
RESOLVED → CLOSED
OPEN → CANCELLED
IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED

Every other transition is invalid, including:

OPEN → OPEN
OPEN → RESOLVED
OPEN → CLOSED
IN_PROGRESS → OPEN
IN_PROGRESS → IN_PROGRESS
IN_PROGRESS → CLOSED
RESOLVED → OPEN
RESOLVED → IN_PROGRESS
RESOLVED → RESOLVED
RESOLVED → CANCELLED
CLOSED → OPEN
CLOSED → any other state
CANCELLED → OPEN
CANCELLED → any other state

Invalid transitions MUST be rejected by the backend.

A newly created ticket ALWAYS starts as OPEN.

The client MUST NOT choose the initial status.

Ticket creation:

- title: required, non-blank
- description: required, non-blank
- priority: required, LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH
- assignee: optional string
- status is not accepted during creation

Ticket update:

Only these fields may be changed:

- title
- description
- priority
- assignee

Status must NOT be changed through the normal ticket field PATCH.

Status changes use the dedicated status operation.

Field updates remain allowed even when ticket status is CLOSED or CANCELLED.

Comments:

- body is required and non-blank
- comments can be added to any existing ticket
- comments are allowed even for CLOSED and CANCELLED tickets
- no authentication/user system
- no comment edit/delete feature

Search:

- keyword search is case-insensitive
- search title and description only
- keyword and status filter can be combined using AND

Status filter:

- single status
- invalid status value returns a meaningful 400 error

Errors:

- validation → 400
- ticket not found → 404
- illegal transition → 409
- meaningful JSON error response
- no authentication
- no 401/403 implementation

Do NOT add:

- authentication
- users table
- roles
- JWT
- notifications
- attachments
- SLA
- pagination
- audit log
- Redis
- Kafka
- microservices
- CQRS
- ETag
- unnecessary infrastructure

Frontend:

- Use the existing frontend if already implemented.
- Do not replace it unnecessarily.

4. VERY IMPORTANT: SINGLE PORT PORTAL
==================================================

The final application must behave like ONE Support Ticket Management Portal.

I do NOT want the final demo to require:

Frontend:
http://localhost:XXXX

Backend:
http://localhost:YYYY

Instead, the user should open ONE URL:

http://localhost:9000

and see the complete Support Ticket Management System.

Configure the application so that Spring Boot serves the built React/Vite frontend as static resources.

Use:

PORT = 9000

Do NOT use ports beginning with 8000.

Do NOT make 8000, 8001, 8080, etc. the final application port.

The final demo URL must be:

http://localhost:9000

API endpoints remain under:

/api/v1/...

Example:

http://localhost:9000/api/v1/tickets

The frontend should call the API using relative paths such as:

/api/v1/tickets

Do not hard-code localhost frontend/backend URLs into the production frontend.

For development, make the project easy to run, but the final integrated demo must work from the single 9000 portal.

5. IMPLEMENT THE WORKING APPLICATION
==================================================

Now implement only what is necessary to satisfy the specifications and assignment.

Backend must support:

1. Create ticket
2. List tickets
3. Get ticket details
4. Update title
5. Update description
6. Update priority
7. Update assignee
8. Add comments
9. List comments where required by the UI
10. Search by keyword
11. Filter by status
12. Change status using the state machine
13. Backend validation
14. Meaningful errors
15. PostgreSQL persistence

Use clean Spring Boot layering.

Recommended structure:

api
application
domain
persistence

Controllers must NOT contain state-machine logic.

The state machine must have one clear domain/service owner.

Repositories must not decide whether a transition is valid.

6. DATABASE
==================================================

Use PostgreSQL for the actual application.

Use environment/configuration for:

- database URL
- username
- password

Never commit real credentials.

Keep H2 configuration for tests if already present or useful.

Use UUIDs if that is already established by the existing data model/spec.

Use proper relationships:

Ticket
  1
  |
  *
Comment

Persist tickets and comments.

Data must survive application restart.

==================================================
7. PRESENTABLE UI
==================================================

The final UI must look like an actual Support Ticket Management Portal, not a raw developer demo.

Keep it simple but polished.

Provide:

Dashboard/List page:

- application title/header
- create ticket button
- keyword search
- status filter
- ticket list/table/cards
- status badge
- priority badge
- assignee
- useful empty state

Create ticket:

- title
- description
- priority
- assignee
- clear validation messages
- no status field

Ticket details:

- ticket information
- current status
- priority
- assignee
- created/updated information if already supported by the spec
- status transition controls
- comments
- add comment form
- update fields
- meaningful API error display

The UI must not pretend an invalid transition is valid.

It may hide unavailable transitions as a UX improvement, but backend remains the authority.

Make the UI visually consistent and professional without adding unnecessary product features.
